title: Next image after the NAT-086 finding: launchd restore/ramdisk mode through a last kernel-command-line token xrd=md0 (launchd's strstr for rd=md0 finds it, XNU's whole-key parser ignores it) so that the boot tasks, including launchd_cache_loader, are skipped; build, derive the session driver, analyser rows R1-R9, tests over XNU's real boot-arg parser and Apple's launchd Boot dictionary, decision draft
acceptance: The kernel command line of the built payload equals NAT-085's with the new tag and one last token xrd=md0 and nothing else changed in the XNU payload; XNU's own pexpert/gen/bootargs.c (compiled on the host with shim headers) returns rd=md1 and xrd=md0 for it; kern.bootargs returns the same string the parser reads (source review of kern_sysctl.c).

The restore-mode reading is documented from the disassembly of the pinned launchd (strstr rd=md0, the Boot dictionary flags: PerformAlways / PerformInRestore tasks only) and the allowed-task list of the analyser equals the Boot dictionary read from the binary. This is source review: whether launchd enters restore mode on the phone is the question of the native task.

A session driver derived from NAT-085's by counted substitutions and an analyser (rows R1-R9) tested over the real NAT-084 and NAT-086 archives (both read R5, the control that the analyser tells a launchd without restore mode from one with it; the restore text itself is hand-written because no run has printed it); mutation pass; decision draft with hashes. Nothing here measures the phone.
